28// Address is a multicast address if the most significant byte in the address is 0x01
29#ifndef ETHER_IS_MULTICAST
30#define ETHER_IS_MULTICAST(addr) (*(addr)&0x01) // is address multicast or broadcast

33//
34// Notes:
35//
36// Setting ebtables rules:
37// -----------------------
38// IEEE1905 multicast packets should not be bridge-fludded by default (only "relayed multicast" packets should be fludded)
39// In order to prevent bridge fludding of IEEE1905 multicast packets the following ebtables configuration should be applied:
40//
41// ebtables -t filter -I FORWARD 1 -p 0x893a --destination 01:80:c2:00:00:13 -j DROP
42//
43// Relayed multicast will be implemented by the IEEE1905 protocol handler (in the Ieee1905Transport class)
44//
45// TODO: need to set ebtables rule at the platform level
46//
47//
48// Modifying GRX350 GSWIP-L configuration:
49// --------------------------------------
50// The GSWIP-L ethernet switch hardware of the GRX350 is configured by default to always forward/flood multicast packets. Flooding all multicast
51// packets between the four Ethernet ports of the GRX350 will break the non-relayed multicast behaviour expected
52// from IEEE1905 devices. In order to avoid this the following command should be issued:
53//
54// switch_cli dev=0 GSW_REGISTER_SET nRegAddr=0x454 nData=1
55//
56// TODO: this could be considered a platform bug that should be solved at the platform level - see https://jira-chd.intel.com/browse/UGW_SW-25961
57//

163// IEEE1905 CMDU header in packed format
164#pragma pack(push, 1)
165 struct Ieee1905CmduHeader {
166 uint8_t messageVersion;
167 uint8_t _reservedField0;
168 uint16_t messageType;
169 uint16_t messageId;
170 uint8_t fragmentId;
171 uint8_t flags;
172 void SetLastFragmentIndicator(bool value)
173 {
174 flags = (flags & ~0x80) | (value ? 0x80 : 0x00);
175 };
176 bool GetLastFragmentIndicator() { return (flags & 0x80); };
177 void SetRelayIndicator(bool value) { flags = (flags & ~0x40) | (value ? 0x40 : 0x00); };
178 bool GetRelayIndicator() { return (flags & 0x40); };
179 };
180#pragma pack(pop)
181
182 // packed TLV struct to help in the parsing of the packet
183#pragma pack(push, 1)
184 struct Tlv {
185 protected:
186 uint8_t tlvType;
187 uint16_t tlvLength;
188
189 public:
190 uint8_t &type() { return tlvType; }
191
192 Tlv *next() { return (Tlv *)((uint8_t *)this + size()); }
193
194 size_t size() { return sizeof(Tlv) + ntohs(tlvLength); }
195 };
196#pragma pack(pop)

265 // According to the ieee1905.1 specification section 8.2.1.1, a 1905.1 management entity shall
266 // transmit a topology discovery message *at least* once every 60 seconds. Since any message from
267 // the neighbor will update it's last_seen, in practice it should be safe to consider it dead and
268 // delete it if 70 seconds have passed.
269 const std::chrono::seconds kMaximumNeighbourAge = std::chrono::seconds(70);
270
271 // de-duplication internal data structures
272
273 static constexpr sMacAddr ieee1905_multicast_addr = {
274 .oct = {0x01, 0x80, 0xc2, 0x00, 0x00, 0x13}};
275 // two IEE1905 packets received from the same src address and with the same messageId
276 // will be considered as duplicate iff they are received within a kMaximumDeDuplicationAge duration.
277 // This duration should be long enough to allow for any buffered/in-transit duplicate packets to be flushed; and
278 // should be short enough to handle the case when a device reboots (and reuses the same messageId).
279 const std::chrono::milliseconds kMaximumDeDuplicationAge = std::chrono::milliseconds(1000);
280
281 // limit the size of the de-duplication map (to prevent memory exhaustion attack)
282 const int kMaximumDeDuplicationThreads = 1024;
283
284 struct DeDuplicationKey {
285 sMacAddr src;
286 sMacAddr dst;
287 uint16_t
288 messageType; // required to distinguish the case of Request / Reply (when the reply carries an out of sync MID)
289 uint16_t messageId;
290 uint8_t fragmentId;
291 };
292 struct DeDuplicationKeyCompare {
293 // implement Compare for the std::map template
294 bool operator()(const DeDuplicationKey &lhs, const DeDuplicationKey &rhs) const
295 {
296 // compare based on src and dst address first then messageId, then fragmentId
297 int srccmp = memcmp(lhs.src.oct, rhs.src.oct, ETH_ALEN);
298 if (srccmp)
299 return srccmp < 0;
300 int dstcmp = memcmp(lhs.dst.oct, rhs.dst.oct, ETH_ALEN);
301 if (dstcmp)
302 return dstcmp < 0;
303 else if (lhs.messageType != rhs.messageType)
304 return lhs.messageType < rhs.messageType;
305 else if (lhs.messageId != rhs.messageId)
306 return lhs.messageId < rhs.messageId;
307 else
308 return lhs.fragmentId < rhs.fragmentId;
309 }
310 };
311 struct DeDuplicationValue {
312 std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point time;
313 };
314 std::map<DeDuplicationKey, DeDuplicationValue, DeDuplicationKeyCompare> de_duplication_map_;
315
316 // de-fragmentation internal data structures
317
318 // two IEE1905 packet fragments received from the same src address and with the same messageId
319 // will be considered as belonging to the same PDU iff they are received within a kMaximumDeFragmentionAge duration.
320 // This duration should be long enough to allow for any buffered/in-transit fragments to arrive; and
321 // should be short enough to handle the case when a device reboots (and reuses the same messageId).
322 const std::chrono::milliseconds kMaximumDeFragmentationAge = std::chrono::milliseconds(1000);
323
324 // limit the size of the de-fragmentation map (to prevent memory exhaustion attack)
325 const int kMaximumDeFragmentationThreads = 16;
326
327 static const size_t kMaximumDeFragmentionSize = (64 * 1024);
328
329 struct DeFragmentationKey {
330 sMacAddr src;
331 uint16_t
332 messageType; // required to distinguish the case of Request / Reply (when the reply carries an out of sync MID)
333 uint16_t messageId;
334 };
335 struct DeFragmentationKeyCompare {
336 // implement Compare for the std::map template
337 bool operator()(const DeFragmentationKey &lhs, const DeFragmentationKey &rhs) const
338 {
339 // compare based on src address first then messageId
340 int srccmp = memcmp(lhs.src.oct, rhs.src.oct, ETH_ALEN);
341 if (srccmp)
342 return srccmp < 0;
343 else if (lhs.messageType != rhs.messageType)
344 return lhs.messageType < rhs.messageType;
345 else
346 return lhs.messageId < rhs.messageId;
347 }
348 };
349 struct DeFragmentationValue {
350 std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point time;
351 uint8_t numFragments = 0;
352 uint8_t buf[kMaximumDeFragmentionSize] = {0};
353 int bufIndex = 0;
354 bool complete = false;
355 };
356 std::map<DeFragmentationKey, DeFragmentationValue, DeFragmentationKeyCompare>
357 de_fragmentation_map_;
358
359 static const int kIeee1905FragmentationThreashold = tlvf::
360 MAX_TLV_SIZE; // IEEE1905 packets (CMDU) should be fragmented if larger than this threashold
361
362 // When fragmenting a message it is expected that only the last fragment will have an END OF MESSAGE TLV.
363 // However, when sending a TLV smaller than then the minimum ethernet frame, a padding is added to the frame.
364 // This padding might cause us having unwanted EOM TLV.
365 static const int kIeee1905FragmentationMinimum = 64 - 2 * 6 /* src, dest MAC */ - 2 /* Type */;
